newsitem.title: USA: NYS Dormitory Auth. plans up to $800 mln bond sale.
newsitem.headline: NYS Dormitory Auth. plans up to $800 mln bond sale.

text.p: A New York State Dormitory Authority official said Tuesday the agency plans to sell up to $800 million of bonds in early March for Mental Health Facilities Corp.

However, the official, who declined to be named, said he did not expect that the entire amount of the bonds, which were approved last week by the state Public Authorities Control Board, would be sold.
"My guess is, it's not that high," he said.

The bonds, which will used to finance construction and refund selected 1987 revenue bonds, will be sold through negotiation. While the top managers have been chosen, the rest of the syndicates has not yet been finalized.
The new money portion of the offering, which could total $250 million or more, will be sold through a team led by Smith Barney, the Authority official said.
And Bear Stearns will head the underwriters for the refunding part of the offering, which was expected to add up to $300 million or more.

Further, the Authority plans to sell around Feb 26 a maximum of $27 million of mortgage, nursing home revenue bonds for the Fairport Baptist Homes, which will be insured by the Federal Housing Agency. First Albany was chosen to lead this syndicate, the official said.

But no date has been set yet for two other offerings by the Authority that also were approved last week by New York State, an up to $37 million offering for Siena College and a maximum sale of $20 million of bonds for New York University.
